title: model-router router sections, contract version 1
description: The three top-level sections of a registry file that model-router validates: `router`, `tasks` and `policy`. `router` is REQUIRED; `tasks` and `policy` are OPTIONAL. The schema covers what model-router accepts: object shape, value types, the closed field set on each section, and the per-array element shape. Cross-reference rules (a rating name that the ratings section does not declare, a route label no model emits, two policies that match the same query) are not expressible in JSON Schema and are reported by the engine's `validateRouterSections` after the schema passes. The file's other sections - `format`, `ratings`, `capabilities`, `meters`, `models` - are owned by model-registry's `registry.schema.json`.

router.description: Router-wide data. `rank` is REQUIRED and orders routes when the query has no known task. `questions` is OPTIONAL and maps a declared capability name to a yes/no question sentence the describe step asks. No other keys are accepted.

rank.description: An ordered list of rating names. Every name should be declared in the registry's `ratings` section; the validator reports the name when it is not. The order is read top to bottom.

questions.description: A capability name to a yes/no question sentence. Every capability should be declared in the registry's `capabilities` section; the validator reports the name when it is not.

tasks.description: Named work needs. A task names a description, a stakes-keyed minimums map, an ordered rank list, an optional needs list, and an optional effort level. The keys are task names; the values follow the `task` shape.

policy.description: Named policies. A policy names a task, a list of stakes levels, an ordered list of route entries, a one-line reason, an optional since date, and an optional spec. The keys are policy names; the values follow the `policy` shape.

task.description: One named work need. `description`, `minimums` and `rank` are REQUIRED. `needs` and `effort` are OPTIONAL.

description.description: A one-line description of the task. The validator rejects a description that contains a line break.

minimums.description: A stakes-keyed map of rating floors. The closed key set is `low`, `normal` and `high`; any other key is reported.

low.description: Floors the task applies at `stakes: low`. Each value is a rating name to a finite number floor.

normal.description: Floors the task applies at `stakes: normal`. Each value is a rating name to a finite number floor.

high.description: Floors the task applies at `stakes: high`. Each value is a rating name to a finite number floor.

rank.description: An ordered list of rating names. The order is read top to bottom.

needs.description: Capability names the task requires. Every name should be declared in the registry's `capabilities` section; the validator reports the name when it is not.

effort.description: A ladder level, in order low < medium < high < xhigh < max. Absent means the `config.json` default applies.

policy.description: One policy. `task`, `stakes`, `routes` and `reason` are REQUIRED. `since` and `spec` are OPTIONAL.

task.description: The task name the policy applies to. The name must match a key in the `tasks` section; the validator reports the name when it does not.

stakes.description: The stakes levels the policy applies to. A non-empty list of `low`, `normal` and/or `high`; an empty list is reported by the validator.

routes.description: An ordered list of route entries. Each entry names a label; an entry may also set an effort level. The label must match a route the registry defines; the validator reports the label when it does not.

route.description: The route label the policy places first. A label has the form `<model key>@<harness>[/<provider>]`.

effort.description: An effort level the policy forces on this route. The level must be on the ladder; the validator reports a level that is not.

reason.description: A one-line reason the policy exists. The validator reports a reason that is not a string.

since.description: A date string the policy was added. The validator does not parse the date; any string is accepted here.

spec.description: The spec condition the policy applies to. Only `settled` is valid; absent means the policy applies to every spec. The validator reports a spec that is not the literal `settled`.
